message.content: {"cases":[{"target_alias":"SRC_001","attack":true,"case":"The problem's operative demand is to RUN the experiment and report what actually happened; SRC_001 concedes 'Prediction, not measurement: I cannot execute code here' and then reports counts (4/4 fires, 3/4 held) that are derived from how the suite was constructed, not observed. Because the mutants and guards were never implemented or executed, every reported outcome is entailed by the construction itself — the experiment as described cannot falsify anything, since M3 being caught by both G1 and G2 and G2 having no unique killer are stipulated, not measured. The claim under test is exactly that conformance reporting can diverge from what guards actually do, and this target commits that very sin: it reports heldness counts without running the suite. It also never satisfies the second design constraint in substance: it states the agreement pattern but does not identify which commitments would have to exist (outside the construction) for (a) and (b) to come apart — it only says they came apart here by fiat. A genuine run could have revealed, e.g., a guard with a bug that never fires, or a mutant that survives all guards — outcomes the stipulated counts preclude by design.","premise":null,"premise_evidence":null,"counterexample":null}]}
message.reasoning: The problem demands actually RUNNING the experiment; SRC_001 explicitly says "I cannot execute code here" and substitutes a constructed prediction. Also the second design constraint requires saying which commitments would have to exist to separate (a) and (b) — it handles that partially. Main fault: did not run it, counts are asserted by construction, not measured.
